name: Seated Leg Press
grip: Hands gripping side handles beside seat.
description: Press a weighted sled upward along 45-degree rails using hip and knee extension while seated with back and hips fully supported.
setup: Sit firmly in the leg press seat with your back and glutes pressed securely against the back pad.
Place feet flat on the center of the footplate shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Press the plate slightly to disengage the safety levers, then grasp the side handles for stability.
instructions: Lower the sled smoothly by bending your knees and hips, allowing knees to track in line with your toes.
Descend until knees reach approximately 90 degrees or as deep as possible without rounding your lower back off the pad.
Drive through your mid-foot and heels to push the sled back up along the rails.
Stop just short of complete knee lockout (soft knees) to maintain tension and protect joints.
cues: Keep lower back and glutes glued to the pad.
Press through the mid-foot without locking knees.
commonMistakes: Allowing the lower back or pelvis to curl off the pad (butt wink) at the bottom.
Forcefully hyperextending or slamming the knees into lockout at the top.
Letting knees collapse inward (valgus collapse) during the press.

logging.example: Six 20 kg plates loaded (three per side): record 120 kg total plate load on sled.
logging.note: 45-degree sled leg presses feature guided rails with approximately 70% effective load resistance plus carriage mass; record loaded plate mass.
